arguments.value: Immunotolerance, Inc. hired Alan Crane as an independent consultant to provide advice and other services when requested by the board. In exchange, Crane was to buy 1,990,000 shares of the company’s common stock for $190, and the company would reimburse approved out-of-pocket expenses, but he would receive no employee benefits. The agreement lasts for four years from the effective date and then renews yearly unless the company gives 90 days’ notice. Crane must keep the company’s confidential information secret, return company materials, and assign to the company any inventions or works created in connection with the services or based on company confidential information. For one year after the consulting period, he may not compete in the defined field of tissue-specific immunosuppression drugs and cell-based therapies and may not solicit the company’s employees. The company may end the agreement for cause, and either side may terminate with notice under the stated terms.
